title: Tech risk-reward turns favorable after rout, Deutsche Bank says - Yahoo Finance
text: Tech risk-reward turns favorable after rout, Deutsche Bank says Roushni Nair October 31, 2026 2 min read ^GSPC -0.38% US500 Investing.com -- Deutsche Bank has upgraded global technology stocks to "overweight" after a sharp market selloff and a retreat in investor positioning improved the sector's risk-reward profile, arguing that much of the concern around AI demand is already reflected in valuations. Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list » The bank's strategists, led by Parag Thatte and Chief Strategist Binky Chadha, said mega-cap growth and technology stocks had underperformed the rest of the S&P 500 by more than 16 percentage points over three weeks. The technology group fell 11% during the period, while the remainder of the benchmark gained almost 6%, pushing relative performance to the bottom of its decade-long trend channel. Deutsche Bank said investor positioning had also retreated from elevated levels to neutral, bringing exposure more closely in line with an anticipated earnings growth rate of around 10%. That compares with earnings growth of about 47% in the third quarter and consensus expectations of 36% by the end of next year. Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks » The bank noted that previous rotations back into technology had delivered an average gain of 32%, outperforming the rest of the S&P 500 by 30 percentage points. The broader benchmark also gained an average 16% over the three months following those rotations. Deutsche Bank pointed to continued strength in corporate earnings beyond technology. Although technology and energy account for approximately three-quarters of expected third-quarter S&P 500 earnings growth of 31%, earnings growth excluding those sectors remains a robust 12%. The median S&P 500 company is expected to deliver growth of 14.4%, close to a two-decade high outside recessionary rebounds. The bank acknowledged risks from potential technology regulation following the US midterm elections and further geopolitical escalation, but argued that equity and oil markets had already priced in substantial uncertainty. Oil prices were approximately 65% above its estimate of medium-term fair value. Deutsche Bank said the recent correction had created a more attractive entry point, although further downside remained possible in the event of another major external shock.
